summary: A shared framework for classical Gan–Gross–Prasad problems, from relevant inclusions and their Bessel models to local packet multiplicities, global period propositions and normalized unitary identities. The plan also connects the classical spectral geometry to distinguished tempered spectra, anisotropic automorphic averages and definite and arithmetic diagonal periods. It keeps conjectural assertions separate from proven ranges, tracks exact normalization and classification hypotheses, and imports trace-comparison, orbit-method and Shimura machinery from their owners.

nodes.title: Relevant Bessel pairs
nodes.statement: Let F be a local field or number field of characteristic zero. Let E=F in the quadratic case, or let E/F be quadratic étale with involution c in the hermitian case. A relevant Bessel pair consists of nondegenerate spaces W⊂V, an integer ℓ≥0, and an isometry W⊥≃𝕳^ℓ⊕Ee with ⟨e,e⟩≠0. Thus dim_E V−dim_E W=2ℓ+1, and W⊥ has maximal Witt index ℓ. Put G=SO(V), H=SO(W) in the quadratic case and G=U(V), H=U(W) in the hermitian case; H acts trivially on W⊥. Retain the inclusion of spaces and the isometry class of the complement as data. For ℓ=0 and split E this includes GL_{m+1}⊃GL_m. Hermitian forms here are linear in their first argument; transport to GN.2 by conjugating its first-argument-antilinear convention.
proofSteps: Import the form and isometry-group carriers; construct only the embedding by extension by the identity on W⊥.
Use a hyperbolic decomposition to retain the anisotropic line, including its norm class.
acceptance: For a norm-one line, U(W)→U(W⊕E) sends h to h⊕1.
In the quadratic case use SO, including determinant one; do not replace it by O.

In the hermitian case Wᵅ ranges over forms of the same rank; in the quadratic case it ranges over forms of the same rank and discriminant, with oriented twisting data retained. This is the image of H¹(F,H) in the twisting data for G×H. Tag each pair by its form data, rather than taking all independent products of pure inner forms or identifying different twists merely because their point groups are abstractly isomorphic.

nodes.title: Bessel subgroup and character
nodes.statement: For a relevant pair with V=W⊕(X⊕X*⊕Ee), dim X=ℓ, choose a complete isotropic flag 0⊂X₁⊂⋯⊂Xℓ=X and a nontrivial additive character ψ_F of F. Let P be its stabilizer in G and N its unipotent radical. The standard simple-root coordinates of N consist of the ℓ−1 adjacent flag coordinates and the final coordinate obtained by pairing n(e) with the last dual flag vector. Compose their sum with ψ_F, using the trace to F in the hermitian case and the fixed form normalization, to get ψ_N. The diagonal H fixes ψ_N; set R=H⋉N and ψ_R(hn)=ψ_N(n). At ℓ=0 set N=1 and ψ_R=1. The attached partition is [(2ℓ+1),1^(dim V−2ℓ−1)]. Auxiliary choices give conjugate model data for the fixed inclusion, with the character transported along that conjugacy.
proofSteps: Import parabolic and unipotent-radical structure. Check that the displayed coordinate sum factors through the appropriate abelianization of N.
Verify H-invariance and the semidirect-product character law; transport under changes of flag and nonzero scalar choices by conjugation.
acceptance: The character is trivial on H and nontrivial in every prescribed simple-root coordinate.
The partition parts sum to dim V, including ℓ=0.

nodes.title: Local Bessel functionals
nodes.statement: For a local field F of characteristic zero, Bessel data (R,ψ_R) and irreducible admissible representations π of G(F), σ of H(F), define B(π,σ)=Hom_R(π⊗σ,ℂ_{ψ_R}), so ℓ((π(g)⊗σ(h))v)=ψ_R(g,h)ℓ(v). Over a nonarchimedean field use the algebraic tensor product of smooth representations. Archimedeanly use Casselman–Wallach smooth globalizations, the completed projective tensor product and continuous linear maps. Its finite dimension m(π,σ) is the Bessel multiplicity. The light algebraic predicate IsBesselFunctional(ρ,χ,L) means ∀r v,L(ρ(r)v)=χ(r)L(v), on an existing representation carrier; it does not assert continuity. For ℓ=0, B(π,σ) identifies with Hom_H(π,σ∨), with the appropriate smooth or continuous dual convention.
proofSteps: Use the imported intertwining-map space rather than introducing a second abstract Hom construction.
For the topological version impose continuity on the completed tensor carrier. For codimension one curry the bilinear functional into the smooth contragredient.
acceptance: Bilinear σ corresponds to σ∨ in branching; replacing σ by σ∨ changes the tensor parameter.
The algebraic predicate alone never supplies an archimedean model.

nodes.statement: Over a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero let π be smooth and put J_{N,ψ}(π)=π/span{π(n)v−ψ_N(n)v}. H acts on this quotient because it normalizes (N,ψ_N). The analogous archimedean algebraic quotient is not substituted for continuous Bessel functionals.

H-invariance of ψ makes the H-action well-defined; uncurry for the inverse.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of Bessel models
nodes.statement: For every relevant orthogonal or unitary Bessel pair over a local field of characteristic zero and irreducible admissible π,σ, m(π,σ)≤1. At archimedean places representations are Casselman–Wallach and functionals continuous. In codimension one this also holds for split GL_{m+1}⊃GL_m: dim Hom_H(π,σ)≤1. No genericity or temperedness is required for this individual-pair bound.
proofSteps: For codimension one apply the invariant-distribution multiplicity-one criteria of AGRS (nonarchimedean) and Sun–Zhu (archimedean); the exact distribution inputs are recorded as gap L1 rather than assumed to follow from Schur’s lemma.
For ℓ>0 use GGP Theorem 15.1 with an auxiliary supercuspidal representation outside the finitely many forbidden Bernstein supports; use its archimedean counterpart for continuous models.
The resulting Hom identification transfers the codimension-one bound.
acceptance: For compact U(2)⊃U(1), each weight in an irreducible restriction has multiplicity one, agreeing with the existing Classical Groups branching theorem.
A zero Hom space is allowed; multiplicity one does not assert nonvanishing.

nodes.title: Local relevant Vogan packets
nodes.statement: Fix a quasi-split relevant pair, Whittaker normalization, and a pair φ=(φ_G,φ_H) of local Langlands parameters for its L-groups. Assume the packet correspondences of ML.4 for the indicated inner forms. Define the relevant Vogan packet as the tagged disjoint union of Π_{φ_G}(Gᵅ)×Π_{φ_H}(Hᵅ) over the relevant pure inner forms of GGP.0; an individual packet can be empty for an inner form to which φ is not relevant. Use actual irreducible representations with their form tags. A generic parameter means its quasi-split packet contains a Whittaker-generic representation, not that every member is generic. Tempered means bounded Weil-group image. When an even-SO supplier gives only outer-conjugacy orbits, retain those orbits and formulate any sharper labeling conditionally on a full normalization; do not select representatives canonically.
proofSteps: Import each individual packet and relevance test from ML.4, including all its classification hypotheses.
Take the disjoint union over twists of the inclusion rather than the Cartesian product of two unrestricted Vogan unions.
acceptance: The packet sum counts the same representation on different retained form data separately only when the twisting equivalence requires it.
No global parameter is required for the local definition.

nodes.title: Coherent global Vogan packets
nodes.statement: For a number field F and generic discrete global parameters φ_G,φ_H, use their localizations and supplied unramified distinguished vectors to form restricted tensor products of members of the local relevant packets. Call such data coherent when there is one global relevant inclusion W⊂V whose localizations are the specified form pairs. The coherent global packet consists of these data together with the global group; its cuspidal automorphic subset further requires an actual cuspidal realization. Local membership does not assert coherence or automorphic occurrence. The latter is tested by the appropriate global multiplicity formula, retaining even-SO outer information and the classification assumptions of ML.4.
proofSteps: Take restricted tensor products with spherical choices at almost all places.
Apply local-to-global form classification for coherence, then the separate global packet multiplicity criterion for occurrence.
acceptance: A global central sign condition is necessary but cannot replace the full multiplicity formula.
Generic discrete automorphic members are used as cuspidal only with the precise supplied cuspidality theorem (gap P2).

nodes.title: Hermitian generic discrete parameters
nodes.statement: For a quadratic extension E/F of number fields and N≥1, a Hermitian generic discrete parameter of rank N is the imported isobaric sum Π=⊞_{i=1}^r Π_i, ΣN_i=N, of pairwise nonisomorphic unitary conjugate-self-dual cuspidal Π_i on GL_{N_i}(𝔸_E), each of sign (−1)^{N−1}. Analytically require L(s,Π_i,As^{(−1)^{N+1}}) to have a pole at s=1. Equivalently its opposite-parity Asai factor As^{(−1)^N} is regular there, using the conjugate-self-dual cuspidal Asai dichotomy (gap F1). The parity uses total N. The associated representation is full normalized induction in the unitary isobaric case. This is a generic discrete Arthur parameter, with all SL₂ multiplicities one, not a general Arthur parameter.
proofSteps: Import isobaric sums from AS.2, not a duplicate induction construction.
Filter the unique multiset of constituents by distinctness, conjugate self-duality and total-rank sign; compare the two parity descriptions via the Asai dichotomy.
acceptance: For r=1 this recovers the stable cuspidal situation.
A repeated constituent is excluded even when the induced representation is irreducible.

nodes.title: Weak unitary base change
nodes.statement: Let π be an irreducible admissible representation of U(V)(𝔸_F) for E/F quadratic, and Π an isobaric automorphic representation on GL_N(𝔸_E). Say Π is a weak base change of π if, at almost every finite place v of F split in E, Π_v equals the split local base change of π_v. With E_v=F_v×F_v this is the pair (π_v,π_v∨), with the two factors interchanged when the chosen place over v is interchanged. The definition alone gives neither existence nor cuspidality of π or Π. For the global period statements restrict Π to a Hermitian parameter and π to a cuspidal realization.
proofSteps: Use the split isomorphism U(V)(F_v)≃GL_N(F_v) and the conjugate-self-dual standard embedding.
State the almost-everywhere relation on isomorphism classes; strong all-place compatibility is a separate classification-dependent theorem.
acceptance: Changing finitely many tested places does not change the condition.
No existence assertion for a merely admissible adelic representation follows from Remark 1.7.

nodes.title: The quasi-split unitary pair

nodes.title: Tempered local absolute convergence
nodes.statement: For all codimension-one orthogonal, unitary and split general-linear GGP pairs over a local field of characteristic zero, ∫_H Ξ_G(h)Ξ_H(h)dh is finite. Consequently the raw period α of GGP.4 is absolutely convergent for smooth vectors in irreducible tempered unitary representations and is continuous in those vectors in their smooth representation topologies. The full proof uses estimates with the required polynomial norm factors as well as the bare Ξ-integrability assertion.
proofSteps: Bound tempered coefficients by Ξ times controlled polynomial norms using AF.1 and SR.3.
Use relative Cartan chambers; compare the half-modulus characters to obtain a strictly decaying exponential in each noncompact chamber direction, with the necessary polynomial weights.
For the split case divide chambers according to where the extra eigenvalue 1 occurs; compact directions contribute finite volume. Orthogonal exponents are supplied by L4.
Use smooth seminorm bounds in the same dominating integrals for continuity.
acceptance: For compact H the integrability is immediate.
The theorem is not applied to arbitrary nontempered representations.

sources.match: States the integrability property and smooth-vector continuity for all three pair types.
Reduces unitary and split GL cases to chamber integrals using matrix-coefficient bounds and modulus exponents.

nodes.title: Normalized unitary local periods
nodes.statement: In the everywhere-tempered unitary setting, with strong parameter-compatible local base change and the finite nonzero local central quotient 𝓛_v(1/2,σ_v), set P_v♮(x,y)=𝓛_v(1/2,σ_v)^{-1}∫_{U(V_n)(F_v)}⟨σ_v(h)x,y⟩_v dh. Use the bilinear product representation σ_v on U(V_n)×U(V_{n+1}); decomposable vectors recover the raw-period convention after dualizing its second factor. The inner product and Haar measure are explicit data. For a global restricted tensor, the product of ratios P_v♮(x_v,x_v)/⟨x_v,x_v⟩_v is defined after the unramified normalization makes almost every ratio one.
proofSteps: Check finiteness and nonvanishing of the local L-quotient by the actual tempered local-factor theorem F1.
Divide the convergent raw form by that nonzero number; establish the restricted product only after the next unramified computation.
acceptance: A rescaling of the local invariant metric cancels in P_v♮(x_v,x_v)/⟨x_v,x_v⟩_v.

nodes.title: The unramified local calculation
nodes.statement: At an unramified place v for E/F, the unitary form pair, and the tempered representations with compatible unramified base change, choose hyperspecial K_n⊂K_{n+1} and nonzero spherical vector x_v. Then P_v♮(x_v,x_v)=vol(U(V_n)(𝒪_v))⟨x_v,x_v⟩_v. In particular the ratio is one when the smaller hyperspecial subgroup has volume one. This includes split and inert unramified places with their respective local factors. It is not a formula for arbitrary ramified fixed vectors.
proofSteps: Use the normalized spherical matrix coefficients and the spherical integral computation of Harris, with the precise unramified integration contract L4.
Identify its Satake factors with 𝓛_v(1/2) and retain the smaller hyperspecial Haar volume.
acceptance: With unit spherical vectors and volume-one hyperspecial H, the value is 1.
At a split place both conjugate-dual tensor factors occur in the E-local L-function.

nodes.title: The unitary Ichino–Ikeda proposition
nodes.statement: For a cuspidal σ on U_h with Hermitian generic discrete base change Π and tempered at every place, define UnitaryIchinoIkeda(σ) to assert, for every nonzero factorizable smooth x=⊗′x_v, |P_h(x)|²/⟨x,x⟩_Pet=|S_Π|^{-1}𝓛(1/2,σ)∏_v[P_v♮(x_v,x_v)/⟨x_v,x_v⟩_v]. Global measures are Tamagawa measures, local Haar factors are a compatible restricted product with its convergence factors, and the global Petersson metric is the stated quotient integral. Almost all smaller hyperspecial volumes are one. Its truth is a theorem in the everywhere-tempered unitary range of BCZ, but that proof belongs to JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison. The definition introduces no axiom.
proofSteps: Package the normalized equality as a proposition with the global and local metrics and measures retained.
Use the unramified calculation to define a finite nontrivial product; no infinite unnormalized product is used.
The theorem contract J1 supplies the proof in the stated range without moving the trace-comparison argument here.
acceptance: For a stable pair the denominator |S_Π| is 4.
The equality is invariant under rescaling a local metric and under rescaling x.

nodes.title: Eigenvalue invariants for standard representations
nodes.statement: For a codimension-one GGP pair over a characteristic-zero field k, extend to an algebraic closure. In the unitary case split k₁⊗k̄=k̄×k̄ and write V=V⁺⊕V⁻ with the perfect pairing between its two factors; in the orthogonal case put V⁺=V⁻=V. For skew-adjoint x∈𝔤 let ev(x) be the multiset of eigenvalues on V⁺, deleting exactly one forced zero if G is odd orthogonal. It depends only on the adjoint-quotient class. For even SO, retain the Pfaffian coordinate as well: ev alone does not distinguish the two regular semisimple SO classes exchanged by an orientation-reversing orthogonal conjugation. Choose the orientation/volume normalization needed to define pf.
proofSteps: Compute eigenvalues after scalar extension; skew-adjointness gives opposite eigenvalues on V⁻.
Use characteristic-polynomial invariance under conjugation, with the classical adjoint quotient supplied by geometry contract O1.
For odd SO remove one zero with its known multiplicity; for even SO keep the independent Pfaffian sign.
acceptance: The multiset size is 2⌊dim V/2⌋ in the orthogonal case and dim_E V in the unitary case.

nodes.title: Eigenvalues detected by isotropic vectors
nodes.statement: Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field in the preceding notation, c∈ev(x) if and only if there is a nonzero isotropic eigenvector of x in V⁺ with eigenvalue c, equivalently a nonzero isotropic eigenvector in V⁻ with eigenvalue −c. In the split unitary case the factors V⁺ and V⁻ are themselves isotropic. In the odd-orthogonal case removing one forced zero is essential to the zero-eigenvalue equivalence.
proofSteps: For c≠0 skew-adjointness gives 2c⟨v,v⟩=0, hence isotropy.

For c=0 in the quadratic case use the Jordan decomposition at zero: an excess zero beyond the forced odd-dimensional line yields an isotropic eigenvector; conversely such a vector forces the adjusted characteristic polynomial to vanish at zero.
For the unitary split factors use the perfect dual pairing to compare opposite eigenvalues.
acceptance: For so₁ at x=0 there is no isotropic nonzero vector and ev is empty.
For so₃ at x=0 the adjusted spectrum contains zero and an isotropic line exists over the algebraic closure.

nodes.title: A regularity criterion for GGP Lie algebras
nodes.statement: Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, suppose every isotropic subspace of V⁺ on which x∈𝔤 acts by a scalar has dimension at most one; in the orthogonal case also suppose dim ker x≤2. Then x is regular, meaning dim Z_𝔤(x)=rank G. This asserts regularity, not regular semisimplicity.
proofSteps: Decompose V into generalized eigenspaces and pair the c and −c pieces. The scalar-isotropic-space hypothesis forces at most one Jordan chain for each nonzero eigenvalue.

On the zero generalized eigenspace use the permitted orthogonal Jordan types and the kernel bound; compare the resulting centralizer dimension with rank. The Jordan/centralizer contract O1 retains the nilpotent cases.
acceptance: Over the algebraic closure the unitary rank-two case is gl₂: a single nilpotent Jordan block satisfies the hypotheses and is regular but not semisimple.
For x=0 on an orthogonal space of dimension at least five the isotropic scalar-space bound fails.

sources.match: Reduces the regularity assertion to Jordan blocks, with the extra orthogonal kernel condition.

nodes.title: The geometric spherical orbit
nodes.statement: For a codimension-one orthogonal, unitary or split-GL GGP pair over characteristic zero, the diagonal algebraic H has a geometric open orbit with trivial stabilizer on the product of complete flag varieties Flag(G)×Flag(H), after extending scalars to an algebraic closure. This is a statement about the full algebraic groups attached to the forms; it neither replaces SO by its real identity component nor asserts an open orbit on all real points.
proofSteps: Over the algebraic closure choose two transverse flags so that any common stabilizer fixes successive pairings with the distinguished vector e.
In the split GL case successive flag-line comparisons make the stabilizer the identity. In the orthogonal case the same argument uses the isotropic flag and orientation, not a lost determinant sign.
Verify dim H=dim Flag(G)+dim Flag(H); the constructed free orbit is therefore open. The explicit flag construction and orthogonal extension are the specialized geometry input O1.
acceptance: For GL₂⊃GL₁ the generic line in ℙ¹ has trivial stabilizer under t↦diag(t,1).
The result is algebraic over k̄, so multiple rational or real open orbits cause no contradiction.

sources.match: States the open flag orbit with trivial stabilizer.
Constructs good minimal parabolics in the unitary model; after scalar extension this yields the flag-orbit calculation.

nodes.title: Archimedean parameter and infinitesimal character
nodes.statement: For an irreducible admissible representation π of a real classical group in the codimension-one GGP setting, write the complex-torus restriction of its Langlands parameter as φ_π(e^t)=exp(tλ_π+t̄μ_π). Under the standard trace-pairing identification between the dual-group adjoint quotient and [𝔤*_ℂ], λ_π maps to π’s Harish–Chandra infinitesimal character. If π is tempered then μ_π=−conj(λ_π). Use the normalized induction convention and the Harish–Chandra ρ shift of AF.1.
proofSteps: Reduce by normalized parabolic induction to discrete series and compact torus data.
Compare highest weights and the ρ shift with the local Langlands normalization; the necessary real classical correspondence remains within P1.
acceptance: The trivial finite-dimensional representation has infinitesimal character ρ under AF.1’s convention; it is not normalized to zero.

sources.match: Checks the parameter-to-infinitesimal-character comparison by normalized induction, discrete series and tori.

nodes.title: Standard tensor weights at a real place
nodes.statement: For a real codimension-one GGP pair and λ,μ the infinitesimal parameters, the infinitesimal weights of the standard Rankin–Selberg L-representation are the multiset ev(λ)+ev(μ) in the orthogonal case, and that multiset together with its negatives in the unitary case. Here + is the pairwise multiset sum with multiplicity. For tempered π,σ the real local factor has form ∏_i Γ_ℝ(s+a_i⁺+ε_i), where a_i are these weights, a⁺=|Re a|+i Im a, and ε_i∈{0,1} is determined by the W_ℝ action, not by ev alone. Contragredience in the branching convention replaces μ by −μ.
proofSteps: Use the standard representations of the dual classical groups and the trace-form comparison to write their eigenvalue multisets.
Tensor products add infinitesimal weights. Restriction of scalars in the unitary case contributes the conjugate-dual weights as well.
Apply the imported real Weil-group local-factor formula with its parity data.
acceptance: For SO₃⊃SO₂ both adjusted multisets have size two, giving four tensor weights.
For U₂⊃U₁ the two pairwise sums and their negatives give four real gamma weights.

nodes.title: Stability and the zero-weight obstruction
nodes.statement: Using spectral stability from the orbit-method owner, a pair (λ,μ) is stable exactly when ev(λ)∩ev(μ)=∅; the geometric GGP stability theorem identifies this with H-stability of an element restricting to those parameters. For real π,σ this is equivalent to zero being absent from the infinitesimal Satake weights of the tensor parameter π×σ∨. Thus on a compact stable rescaled parameter set the archimedean conductor has the full predicted power of the scaling parameter. This is a zero-weight obstruction statement, not a claim that every nonstable pair has zero period.
proofSteps: Import the geometric stable-locus theorem from the orbit-method owner through O1; do not redevelop GIT stability here.
By the weight comparison, zero occurs in ev(λ)−ev(μ) exactly when the two adjusted spectra meet.
On a compact stable set all these differences are uniformly bounded away from zero, giving uniform conductor scaling.
acceptance: For SO₃⊃SO₂ with parameters {±a} and {±b}, spectral stability means a≠±b.
The compactness hypothesis is necessary for a uniform lower bound on the weight differences.

sources.locator: Theorem 14.2 and Definition 14.3, p. 97; Lemma 15.4, p. 107

nodes.title: The distinguished tempered spectrum
nodes.statement: For a codimension-one GGP pair over a local field of characteristic zero and a fixed irreducible tempered unitary π of G, let Ω_π={σ∈Ĥ_temp:Hom_H(π^∞,σ^∞)≠0}. Take isomorphism classes of σ, using smooth maps in the nonarchimedean setting and continuous maps of smooth globalizations at archimedean places. This is a subset of the supplied tempered dual, not a new construction of that dual. The branching convention is Hom_H(π,σ), hence the bilinear local Bessel model uses σ∨.
proofSteps: Form the subset using the supplied representation category and Hom space.
Keep the smooth topology in the Hom predicate; neither an algebraic Hom nor a Hilbert-bounded map replaces it.
acceptance: A compact branching constituent belongs precisely when its existing Classical Groups branching multiplicity is one.

nodes.title: Support of the tempered local period
nodes.statement: For a nonarchimedean characteristic-zero codimension-one GGP pair of orthogonal, unitary or split GL type and tempered irreducible π,σ, the convergent raw local form B on π⊗σ∨ is nonzero iff Hom_H(π,σ)≠0. Equivalently the relative character H_σ supplied by the orbit-method roadmap is nonzero iff σ∈Ω_π. The same nonvanishing equivalence holds for the real unitary pairs covered by BP20. This last extension alone does not assert positivity at real places.
proofSteps: Invariance shows a nonzero raw form gives a nonzero model functional.
For the converse use the tempered model nonvanishing theorem, through local analytic contract L4; in codimension one its regularized integral is the ordinary convergent integral.
The relative-character expansion has the same support, using the basis and positivity contracts of its owner.
acceptance: For compact H, integration projects onto the matching representation and detects exactly the existing branching constituent.
No nontempered integral is asserted convergent.

nodes.title: Positivity of nonarchimedean GGP periods
nodes.statement: For tempered irreducible unitary π,σ of a nonarchimedean characteristic-zero codimension-one GGP pair, B(x,x)≥0 for every smooth x∈π⊗σ∨, and the supplied relative character satisfies H_σ(v,v)≥0. In particular α(v,v;u,u)≥0. Positivity is a theorem in this range; at archimedean places it remains an explicit condition wherever the chosen sources have not established it. This is positivity of the integrated form, not pointwise positivity of the integrand.
proofSteps: Apply the supplied positive spectral/model factorization L4/O2 for this nonarchimedean spherical pair.
Evaluate the rank-one positive form on decomposable tensors and then sum the diagonal terms in the relative-character expansion; absolute convergence permits the sum.
acceptance: For compact H this is the nonnegative orthogonal projection norm.
A unitary coefficient may take negative or nonreal pointwise values, so positivity is not obtained by pointwise comparison.

nodes.title: Phase normalization of distinguished intertwiners
nodes.statement: Assume the supplied relative character H_σ on π^∞ is a continuous positive semidefinite Hermitian form, with its local period factorization, and that Hom_H(π^∞,σ^∞) has dimension at most one. If H_σ≠0, choose ℓ_σ:π^∞→σ^∞ so that H_σ(v₁,v₂)=⟨ℓ_σ(v₁),ℓ_σ(v₂)⟩ and B(v₁⊗bar(u₁),v₂⊗bar(u₂))=⟨ℓ_σ(v₁),u₁⟩overline(⟨ℓ_σ(v₂),u₂⟩). The choice is unique up to a unit complex scalar. Set ℓ_σ=0 when H_σ=0. The positive factorization and smooth-target existence are inputs O2/L4; a general GNS construction alone does not identify that target with σ. Positivity is known in the nonarchimedean range; at other places it is an explicit hypothesis.
proofSteps: Use the supplied positive rank-one period factorization and the one-dimensional Hom space.
Scale any nonzero intertwiner by the positive square root of its scalar ratio to H_σ; retain its residual unit phase.
Use the smooth-target continuity supplied by O2, not an unsupported claim that the operator is bounded on Hilbert completions.
acceptance: The normalization of a nonzero ℓ_σ fixes its norm but never chooses a preferred phase.

nodes.title: Multiplicity one for induction parameters
nodes.statement: Over a nonarchimedean field, let 𝒟_H be the tempered induction-parameter space of conjugacy classes of square-integrable data (M,τ), modulo the finite equivalence relation for normalized unitary induction, and l:Ĥ_temp→𝒟_H its supplied map. Its restriction l|Ω_π is injective. Equivalently any full normalized induction of a square-integrable representation of a Levi of H has at most one π-distinguished irreducible summand, and that summand occurs with branching multiplicity one. Use the precise full-induction multiplicity statement, not only individual irreducible uniqueness.
proofSteps: The R-group/tempered induction contract S1 puts each fiber of l in a single tempered L-packet.
Apply the relevant-packet GGP multiplicity-one theorem, retaining its local classification conditions and even-SO convention.
Alternatively the direct full-induction theorem cited in the source supplies the same conclusion through L2/S1; it must not be inferred from irreducible multiplicity one alone.
acceptance: For compact H each irreducible is its own inducing datum, and the restricted injection is immediate.
No injection on all of Ĥ_temp is claimed.

sources.match: Separates the injection on the distinguished locus from the possible noninjectivity on the whole tempered dual and names the full-induction input.

nodes.title: Topology of the distinguished nonarchimedean spectrum
nodes.statement: With the supplied tempered induction-parameter topology, l(Ω_π) is a union of whole l-components. Each component is a finite quotient of a compact real torus of unitary unramified twists. Transporting this topology along the preceding injection makes Ω_π a disjoint union of those quotients; the relative characters H_σ vary continuously there, and Ω_π→Spec(Bernstein center of H) is continuous. For a sufficiently small good compact open J, Ω_π^J is a finite union of such components. No equality with the Fell-subspace topology is asserted.
proofSteps: Use the full-induction formula for H_σ and smoothness of test vectors to prove continuity in each unitary unramified twist parameter (contract S1/O2).
Upper semicontinuity of multiplicity makes the distinguished subset closed, while local nonvanishing of the continuously varying character makes it open.
The connected torus quotient is therefore entirely in or out; transport its topology and the Bernstein-center map.
Uniform admissibility for good J bounds the number of components meeting J-fixed vectors.
acceptance: A compact H gives a discrete distinguished spectrum; every singleton component is open.
The topology used for auxiliary spectral windows is this explicit l-topology.

sources.match: Uses upper semicontinuity of distinction and continuity of the full-induction relative character to obtain entire components and their topology.

nodes.title: Finite spectral weights for a compact subgroup
nodes.statement: When H is compact, every finitely supported k:Ω_π→ℂ is realized by a finite-rank smooth tensor T∈π⊗bar(π) with H_σ(T)=k(σ) for all irreducible σ of H, extended by zero off Ω_π. If k≥0, T can be chosen positive semidefinite. Its normalization uses the specified Haar measure and relative character. This is a specialization of the supplied compact decomposition and character, not a second Peter–Weyl theorem.
proofSteps: Apply the existing compact isotypic decomposition and GGP multiplicity one.
In each of the finitely many selected isotypic summands choose smooth vectors and normalize their rank-one character value to one.
Sum the resulting tensors with coefficients k(σ); nonnegative coefficients give a positive semidefinite tensor.
acceptance: For the standard U(2) restricted to U(1), weights on characters 1 and z are realized by a diagonal 2×2 operator.

sources.match: Uses the compact multiplicity-free restriction to realize finite spectral weights by smooth finite-rank tensors.

nodes.title: Anisotropic automorphic branching data
nodes.statement: Fix a number field F and a codimension-one pair (G,H)=(U_{n+1},U_n), n≥1, or (SO_{n+1},SO_n), n≥2, both anisotropic over F. Choose an archimedean q where G(F_q) is quasi-split, with G(F_v) compact at every other archimedean v. Choose finite R containing all archimedean and bad places, compatible smooth integral models and hyperspecial K_v⊃J_v outside R, and G(F)G_RK=G(𝔸), H(F)H_RJ=H(𝔸). Factor Tamagawa measures with vol(K)=vol(J)=1. Fix an actual square-integrable automorphic embedding Π⊂L²([G]), unramified outside R, such that Π_R=π⊗π′ is tempered and π=Π_q is generic. Use all actual automorphic copies Σ⊂L²([H]) unramified outside R when summing. The geometric setup has τ(G)=τ(H)=2; the group-specific volume theorem A1 is retained as an input.
proofSteps: Package the existing adelic quotient, restricted tensor product and chosen automorphic embedding, retaining the integral models and measures.
Use anisotropy for compactness and the group-specific Tamagawa theorem for the value 2; neither compactness nor the numerical volume is automatic from the Haar construction alone.
acceptance: The split GL pair is a local comparison case but is excluded from this anisotropic global setup.

nodes.title: Global branching coefficients
nodes.statement: For the preceding data and an actual Σ with Π_R,Σ_R tempered and distinguished, let p(v,bar(u))=∫_[H]v(h)overline(u(h))dh. It gives P(x,y)=p(x)overline(p(y)) on smooth Π_R⊗Σ_R∨. Let B_R be the convergent product-representation local form on this tensor carrier, using the slot exchange in GGP.4. When B_R is nonzero and positive semidefinite, multiplicity one gives a unique scalar L_R(Π,Σ)≥0 such that P=L_R(Π,Σ)B_R. If distinction fails, set L_R=0. In the remaining distinguished case the coefficient is defined only after the nonzero positive form has been supplied; its existence is an explicit local input in the family theorems. It depends on R, the fixed global embedding, and the compatible metrics and measures.
proofSteps: Integrate the global smooth vectors on the compact [H].
Use the one-dimensional local invariant-functional space to compare the two Hermitian forms. Positivity makes the scalar nonnegative and nonvanishing makes it unique.
Keep the chosen automorphic copy: an abstract representation with two embeddings need not have the same period.
acceptance: If the global period vanishes while B_R≠0, the coefficient is zero.

sources.match: Defines the coefficient by comparing the squared global period with the local invariant form; the nonzero local-form hypothesis is visible.

nodes.title: The refined proposition with R-factors removed
nodes.statement: For tempered distinguished Π_R,Σ_R in GGP.7, define RemovedPlaceRefinement(Π,Σ,R) to assert that B_R is nonzero positive and that L_R(Π,Σ)=2^{-β(Π,Σ)}Δ_G^{(R)}L^{(R)}(1/2,Π×Σ∨)/L^{(R)}(1,Ad,Π×Σ∨). Here 2^β is the order of the Arthur-parameter centralizer component group in the convention of the refined period identity, the denominator is the product adjoint factor, and Δ_G^{(R)} has almost-everywhere local factor q_v^{dim G}/#G(𝔽_v). All factors at R are removed, including archimedean factors. This is a proposition, not an assumed theorem. In unitary everywhere-tempered cases its truth follows from the supplied Ichino–Ikeda theorem after reconciling Haar and dual conventions. No universal equality 2^β=τ(G)τ(H) is asserted.
proofSteps: Package the removed-place identity with its local nonvanishing and positivity conditions.
For the known unitary comparison, dualize Σ, remove the R-factors from the completed formula and compare the same global measure and automorphic metric.
Use the actual component group order, including endoscopic constituents; do not replace it by a generic volume prediction.
acceptance: For a stable unitary pair the group order is 4; an endoscopic pair with three total constituents has order 8.

sources.match: Separates the precise component-group normalization from a generic expectation involving Tamagawa volumes.

nodes.title: Admissible automorphic branching families
nodes.statement: For GGP.7 let 𝒪 be the nonempty regular-nilpotent limit orbit set of the generic π, with stable restriction image X=[𝔥^]∩image(𝒪_stab) supplied by the orbit-method owner. Choose nonempty open precompact U⊂X of zero-boundary affine measure, and nonempty open precompact U′⊂Ω_{π′} of zero-boundary Plancherel measure in the supplied distinguished topology. At every finite v∈R the projection of U′ must lie in a union of allowable l-components, in the exact two positive approximation senses of NV Definition 24.3. Define ℱ_h, for h>0, to be the actual automorphic copies Σ unramified outside R whose σ=Σ_q and σ′=Σ_{R\{q}} are tempered, whose local orbit-intersection 𝒪_{π,σ} is nonempty, with hλ_σ∈U and σ′∈U′. The measures have full support on these loci; retain vol(U)vol(U′)>0 for division in the mean theorem. Let d be the complex dimension of a Borel of (Res_{F_q/ℝ}H)_ℂ. For real q this is the usual absolute Borel dimension; for complex q it is twice that dimension. It is not the flag-variety dimension.
proofSteps: Import stable orbits, affine quotient measure and allowable approximation classes through O1–O3; keep these definitions with their existing owner.
Form the spectral subset with all four restrictions, then use compact-quotient spectral discreteness and precompact windows to obtain finiteness.
Use full-support affine/Plancherel measures for positivity of volumes, rather than assuming every nonempty measurable set has positive measure.
acceptance: For H=U(1), d=1; for H=SO(2), d=1. Both tori have zero-dimensional flag varieties, so substituting that dimension changes the asymptotic.

sources.match: Defines the positive local approximation condition and the precise open spectral windows and orbit-distinguished automorphic family.

nodes.title: The weighted automorphic period limit
nodes.statement: For the anisotropic data and admissible family of GGP.7, with the supplied nonzero positive local forms and quantitative orbit-method inputs O1–O3, h^d∑_{Σ∈ℱ_h}L_R(Π,Σ) tends to [τ(H)/τ(G)]vol(U)vol(U′) as h→0⁺. In the exceptional pair (SO₃,SO₂), write K=F(√(−disc V_H)) and χ=η_{K/F}∘θ using the spinor norm θ; impose Π≄Π⊗χ. This is the correction to the source’s stated weighted theorem recorded as E1. The theorem does not use the refined L-value proposition.
proofSteps: Apply the supplier’s limit-state equidistribution theorem to smooth archimedean symbols and allowable auxiliary weights, with the non-self-twist correction in the rank-one orthogonal exception.
Use the two positive approximation bounds at finite places and smooth approximation of zero-boundary windows.
Control both upper and lower errors by their small affine/Plancherel integrals, obtaining the displayed sharp-window limit.
acceptance: In the stated setup τ(H)/τ(G)=1, so the limit is the product of the two window volumes.
The dihedral self-twist case is excluded from this equality, rather than silently counted with the same constant.

sources.match: Transfers limit-state equidistribution through positive approximation to unweighted windows; the SO₃/SO₂ condition repairs the identified obstruction.

nodes.title: The family Weyl law
nodes.statement: For the same anisotropic data and admissible windows, h^d|ℱ_h|→τ(H)vol(U)vol(U′)>0 as h→0⁺. This counting theorem does not require Π≄Π⊗χ in the SO₃/SO₂ case. It counts actual automorphic copies and uses the stated Tamagawa normalization.
proofSteps: Use the supplier’s local smooth spectral approximation and the compact trace specialization of AS.6.
At the distinguished real place shrink geometric support so that only the identity contributes. Evaluate that contribution with quotient volume τ(H).
Apply the zero-boundary approximation to pass to ℱ_h; retain positivity to obtain eventual nonemptiness.
acceptance: The ratio |ℱ_h|h^d/[vol(U)vol(U′)] tends to 2 in this setup.
The SO₃/SO₂ self-twist does not change this counting normalization.

sources.match: Obtains the count from the compact trace formula, with the identity geometric term dominating the shrinking test support.

nodes.title: Analytic conductor and family size
nodes.statement: Uniformly for Σ∈ℱ_h as h→0⁺, the analytic conductor of L(s,Π×Σ∨) at s=1/2 satisfies C(Π,Σ)≍h^{-4d}≍|ℱ_h|⁴. For real q, the exponent at the distinguished place is εm_Gm_H, where (ε,m_G,m_H,d) equals (2,n+1,n,n(n+1)/2) for U_{n+1}/U_n; (1,2n+2,2n,n(n+1)) for SO_{2n+2}/SO_{2n+1}; and (1,2n,2n,n²) for SO_{2n+1}/SO_{2n}. In every displayed real case εm_Gm_H=4d. For complex q, restriction of scalars doubles both d and the gamma-weight count, so the exponent remains 4d; the complex local-factor comparison is part of F1. Contributions away from q stay bounded above and below by the fixed auxiliary windows and unramified conditions.
proofSteps: Apply the real local-factor weight description on the compact closure of the stable window to obtain a positive lower bound for every rescaled tensor weight.
Multiply all gamma-weight sizes and bound the fixed auxiliary-place conductor factors.
Compute the three displayed exponent identities and insert the family Weyl law.
acceptance: For U₂/U₁ and SO₃/SO₂ one has d=1 and C≍h^{-4}.
Allowing the window to meet the zero-weight locus can drop the conductor exponent.

sources.match: Uses uniform stable weight separation and the Borel-dimension identity to compare conductor with the fourth power of family cardinality.

nodes.title: The mean branching coefficient theorem
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of the corrected weighted-period limit, |ℱ_h|^{-1}∑_{Σ∈ℱ_h}L_R(Π,Σ)→1/τ(G)=1/2. If RemovedPlaceRefinement holds for the family, then |ℱ_h|^{-1}∑_{Σ∈ℱ_h}[τ(G)τ(H)/2^{β(Π,Σ)}]Δ_G^{(R)}L^{(R)}(1/2,Π×Σ∨)/L^{(R)}(1,Ad,Π×Σ∨)→τ(H)=2. The component-group factor remains inside the sum when it varies with Σ.
proofSteps: Divide the two limits using the strictly positive window-volume product.
Under the refined proposition substitute its equality termwise, retaining the actual β(Π,Σ), and multiply by τ(G)τ(H).
acceptance: The mean period coefficient is 1/2; it is not 2. The latter is the differently normalized L-value mean.

sources.match: Divides the weighted asymptotic by the family count, and conditionally rewrites it using the refined period identity.

nodes.title: Weak subconvexity for branching coefficients
nodes.statement: In the anisotropic setup of GGP.7, for tempered orbit-distinguished Σ with auxiliary components in fixed allowable compact windows and rescaled distinguished parameters in a fixed compact stable set, L_R(Π,Σ)=o(C(Π,Σ)^{1/4}) as C→∞. This endpoint also holds in the SO₃/SO₂ self-twist case, using the corrected proof’s uniform factor-two bound in place of the false weighted equality. Translating this assertion into an L-value bound additionally requires the removed-place refined proposition and the stated adjoint/component factors. No fixed power saving is asserted.
proofSteps: Use nonnegativity to bound an individual coefficient by a sum over a small window containing its limiting stable parameters.
The uniform positive-window estimate supplied by O3 bounds that sum by h^{-d} times its arbitrarily small volume; in the SO₃/SO₂ exception a bounded factor 2 suffices.
First take the semiclassical limit with the window fixed, then shrink its volume; compactness gives a subsequence argument for the uniform little-o statement.
Use C^{1/4}≍h^{-d}. A single fixed-window mean alone would give only a bounded ratio.
acceptance: The claimed ratio L_R/C^{1/4} tends to zero along every such sequence.
This gives no explicit δ>0 in a bound C^{1/4−δ}.

sources.match: Uses positive local windows and equidistribution to obtain a little-o improvement over the convexity-size period bound; E1 records the correction required in the self-twist exception.

nodes.title: Arithmetic unitary period data
nodes.statement: Let E/F be a CM extension with F totally real and a chosen complex embedding over a real place τ∞. Fix n≥2, the even and odd members n₀=2r₀,n₁=2r₁+1 of {n,n+1}, with r₀,r₁≥1 and n=r₀+r₁. For α=0,1 let Π_α be a conjugate-self-dual cuspidal representation of GL_{nα}(𝔸_E) whose component at each complex place is the irreducible normalized principal series with characters arg^{1−nα},arg^{3−nα},…,arg^{nα−1}, arg(z)=z/|z|. Retain the supplied strong coefficient field L⊂ℂ, its integer ring 𝒪_L, the finite set S_min of ramified and bad places from the two representations and E/F, and the unramified Hecke characters φ_{Πα}:𝕋_{nα}^{S_min}→𝒪_L. A standard definite hermitian space has signature (N,0) at every real place; a standard indefinite one has signature (N−1,1) at τ∞ and (N,0) elsewhere. Write V_{n+1}=V_n⊕E with the fixed positive norm line, and use the supplied neat level pairs K_n⊂K_{n+1}∩U(V_n)(𝔸_f) and their map sh↑. These arithmetic realizations are supplied by the unitary Shimura owner U1, not constructed again here.
proofSteps: Specialize the supplied automorphic and Hecke data to the displayed weights and consecutive ranks.
Use the norm-line inclusion from GGP.0; import the arithmetic quotient, strong coefficient field and neat-level map rather than giving alternate moduli definitions.
acceptance: The adjective relevant for Π here means the displayed regular algebraic cuspidal condition; it is distinct from relevance of a pair of spaces.

sources.locator: Definition 1.1.3 and Remark 1.1.4, p. 110; Definitions 3.1.11, 3.2.1 and 3.2.5, pp. 143–145; §7.1, p. 286
sources.match: Fixes the particular relevant archimedean weights, rank parity, coefficient field, form signatures and compatible arithmetic levels used by the two endpoints.

nodes.title: Finite diagonal periods
nodes.statement: For finite sets S,T, a map ι:S→T and a function f:S×T→ℂ define DiagonalPeriod(ι,f)=∑_{s∈S}f(s,ι(s)). Over a coefficient ring replace ℂ by that ring. On standard definite unitary Shimura sets take S=Sh(V_n,K_n), T=Sh(V_{n+1},K_{n+1}), and ι=sh↑. If n₀=n+1 rather than n, swap the two factors when evaluating a function on Sh(V_{n₀})×Sh(V_{n₁}). The finite-sum definition uses existing finite carriers and sums; it does not define a Shimura set.
proofSteps: Use the finite sum over S and composition with its graph map; prove the API with the existing sum laws.
For Shimura sets import finiteness and sh↑ from U1 and explicitly transport the factor order.
acceptance: For pure tensors f(s,t)=a(s)b(t) this is ∑_s a(s)b(ι(s)), with no complex conjugation.

sources.match: Uses a sum along the graph of the finite-set inclusion, with an integral Hecke-isotypic function on the two factors.

nodes.title: Definite periods as finite graph sums
nodes.statement: For standard definite V_n⊂V_{n+1} and the supplied neat level pair, the global bilinear unitary period on level-fixed functions is c_K times the finite diagonal period, with a single nonzero positive real volume c_K depending on the quotient measure and level. For general non-neat levels the correct sum instead has weights 1/|Γ_s|, where Γ_s is the finite arithmetic stabilizer; an unweighted sum is not asserted there. At neat level all Γ_s are trivial, giving the common volume. Therefore nonvanishing of the global period is equivalent to nonvanishing of the finite sum at these levels.
proofSteps: Decompose U(V_n)(F)\U(V_n)(𝔸) into its finitely many level double cosets.
Integrate the constant value of the level-fixed function over each piece; its volume is a common positive factor divided by the finite stabilizer order.
Apply neatness to remove stabilizers and identify the bilinear product with the graph evaluation in the correct rank order.
acceptance: A singleton neat Shimura set has period c_K times the one graph value.
Unequal stabilizer orders at non-neat levels require weights.

sources.match: Passes from a compact definite unitary period to a finite Shimura-set graph sum at its prescribed levels.

nodes.title: Central values and definite diagonal periods
nodes.statement: For the arithmetic data of GGP.8, if the completed Rankin–Selberg value L(1/2,Π₀×Π₁) is nonzero, there exist a standard definite rank-n space V_n°, a self-dual lattice Λ_n° away from S_min and infinity, V_{n+1}°=V_n°⊕E and Λ_{n+1}°=Λ_n°⊕𝒪_E, and a supplied neat compatible level pair with K_{nα}° hyperspecial equal to U(Λ_{nα}°)(𝒪_v) outside S_min, such that DiagonalPeriod(sh↑,f)≠0 for some f in 𝒪_L[Sh(V_{n₀}°,K_{n₀}°)][ker φ_{Π₀}]⊗_{𝒪_L}𝒪_L[Sh(V_{n₁}°,K_{n₁}°)][ker φ_{Π₁}]. The bracket denotes the Hecke eigenspace annihilated by the indicated kernel. At bad finite places the compact open factors are chosen as part of the conclusion. This is the period endpoint of LTX Lemma 8.2.1, without its subsequent Selmer-group applications.
proofSteps: Apply the stable cuspidal global GGP theorem J1 to the Hermitian pair Π₀⊠Π₁, using its actual cuspidal hypotheses.
At every real place the unique distinguished local pair for these weights is the trivial representation of the compact unitary pair, so the global forms are standard definite.
Use the unramified refinement to obtain self-dual lattices and hyperspecial fixed vectors outside S_min. Choose sufficiently small compatible neat levels at the remaining places.
Identify the compact global period with the finite graph sum and clear coefficient-field denominators within its Hecke eigenspace; the nonzero sum survives.
acceptance: For n=2 the endpoint is a nonzero finite diagonal sum for ranks 2 and 3, not a cycle on a positive-dimensional definite variety.
The lattice and hyperspecial conditions outside S_min are part of the conclusion.

sources.match: Derives the definite graph-sum nonvanishing from the stable global unitary GGP theorem and its unramified-level refinement.
Provides the stable cuspidal realization with nonzero period and permits the stated unramified local choices.

nodes.title: The weak arithmetic GGP proposition
nodes.statement: For the same arithmetic Π₀,Π₁ define WeakArithmeticGGP(Π₀,Π₁) to be the following implication: if L(1/2,Π₀×Π₁)=0 and L′(1/2,Π₀×Π₁)≠0, there exist a standard indefinite V_n, its fixed positive-line extension V_{n+1}, self-dual lattices away from S_min and infinity, and a neat compatible level pair hyperspecial there, such that the graph of sh↑ is nonzero in CH^n(Sh(V_{n₀},K_{n₀})×_E Sh(V_{n₁},K_{n₁}))_L/(ker φ_{Π₀},ker φ_{Π₁}). The notation is the quotient by the sum of the two Hecke-kernel actions, not a choice of an idempotent when none is supplied. The Shimura product has dimension 2n−1 and the graph dimension n−1, hence graph codimension n. Its graph class is imported from MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles and U1. The proposition asserts Chow nonvanishing, and does not assert nonvanishing of an Abel–Jacobi realization. No λ appears in this coefficient-field Chow assertion.
proofSteps: Use the supplied standard indefinite Shimura varieties, their dimension theorem and level map.
Import the graph correspondence, regard it in codimension n, and form the stated Hecke quotient with coefficient field L.
Package the implication as a proposition. Its proof remains conjectural; no arithmetic GGP theorem or Abel–Jacobi injectivity is assumed.
acceptance: For n=2 the graph has dimension one in a three-dimensional product and belongs to CH².
A nonzero Chow class need not have nonzero Abel–Jacobi image without an additional theorem.

sources.locator: Conjecture 8.3.1 and discussion before Theorem 8.3.2, p. 315
sources.match: States the derivative-to-Chow-class conjecture; the subsequent Abel–Jacobi nonvanishing hypothesis is a separate condition.
